caption:
Start database selection with the queries and guarantees your workload needs. Order ID lookups, customer-date ranges and related records can need different data shapes or indexes. SQL/NoSQL labels alone do not determine consistency or transaction support.

Test representative reads and writes before choosing.
#systemdesign #beyondlocalhost
cover_title: Choose the query before the DB

takeaway: Compare exact query and range access patterns
Verify engine transaction and consistency guarantees
Test representative reads writes and operational costs

scenes.title: Same order. Different search.
scenes.narration: An indexed lookup finds order forty-two. A full scan checks rows until it finds a match.
scenes.note: Illustrative query plans, not a benchmark.

scenes.title: Write the query first
scenes.narration: Start with the actual query: fetch one order by identifier. Record its required freshness, traffic pattern, and failure tolerance.
scenes.note: Begin with query behavior and required guarantees.

scenes.title: One query is not enough
scenes.narration: Next, list orders for one customer by date. That access pattern needs a different key or index than a single identifier.
scenes.note: Compare identifier lookups with customer-date queries.

scenes.title: Relational fit
scenes.narration: Relational storage can combine related rows and transaction rules. Choose it when those guarantees and flexible queries fit your order workload.
scenes.note: Check the actual engine and transaction requirements.

scenes.title: Key or document?
scenes.narration: A key-value model fits direct key lookups. A document model can keep an order and its related details together for retrieval.
scenes.note: Document shape should match the required retrieval.

scenes.title: Design around access
scenes.narration: A wide-column model groups rows around partition and clustering keys. Design those keys around the queries the order service actually needs.
scenes.note: Partition and clustering keys shape row access.

scenes.title: Check the price of an index
scenes.narration: An index adds write and storage overhead. SQL and NoSQL labels alone do not specify transaction support or consistency guarantees.
scenes.note: Verify guarantees for the chosen engine and settings.

scenes.title: Test your real workload
scenes.narration: Compare your queries, required guarantees, and operational burden. Test representative reads and writes before choosing the database behind order forty-two.
scenes.note: Evaluate access patterns, guarantees and operations.
